title: smalldocs 0.5.9
subtitle: Reference pages for Rust, TypeScript and HTTP APIs
date: 2026-11-12
author: Rahul Dave
categories: [release]
image: ../images/mark.svg
---

smalldocs can now make reference pages for three more kinds of code. Before, it read Python only. The
key `language` in the `api` section chooses the kind:

- **`rust`** reads a crate, through the JSON that rustdoc writes. It needs a nightly toolchain of Rust.
- **`typescript`** reads a package or an app, through the JSON that TypeDoc writes. It needs Node.
- **`openapi`** reads the OpenAPI document of an HTTP API, from a file, from a command, or from a
  FastAPI app.

The pages look like the Python pages, with a heading, a source link, a code block and a table for each
entry. `smalldocs api check` reports each gap in the comments, as it does for Python. On these sites, a
name in backticks links to its entry when it is a key of `_symbols.json`, even when it does not look like code.

`api` can also be a list of sections, for several references in one site. Each section has its own
`out` folder. `smalldocs api build --out NAME` builds one section of the list.

[Rust, TypeScript and HTTP references](../guide/api-languages.qmd) says how to set up each one. The
front end of cricsdb, in TypeScript, is the first site with one of these references.

## What changes for a site that uses none of it

A site whose `api` is one Python section builds its reference pages as before. Three other changes can
touch any site:

- **A key that an `api` section does not read gives a warning.** For example, `entry` in a Python
  section gives "entry is not read for python; it is for typescript". So `render --strict` now fails on
  such a key, and on `package` beside `packages`. Remove the key, or fix its name.
- **A sidebar entry `auto` with a glob that starts in a folder, such as `auto: api/**`, makes no section
  for that folder, and leaves out its index page,** as Quarto does. The folders inside it are still
  sections. To keep the index in the sidebar, list it
  by name before the `auto` entry. A glob such as `contents: api/*` does not change.
- **An escaped dash or dot is never part of a dash or an ellipsis,** as in Pandoc. The same holds for a character
  reference, such as `&#45;&#45;`. Before, smalldocs made
  `\-\-` an en dash and `\.\.\.` an ellipsis. A heading that has one gets a new id, so a link to
  it must change. For example, the id of `## Head \-\- one` was `#head-one`, and it is now `#head----one`.
